title: Policy Studio: Visual editor for routing by region/tiers and fallback models
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a customer-facing Policy Studio inside the Redwood Console that lets teams author, validate, and preview smart routing policies. Policies should express region selection (preferred/required regions), tier-based routing (hosted/dedicated/private, customer tiers), and fallback model variants (quantized or smaller models, lower-cost variants). The editor must enforce syntactic/semantic validation, show estimated latency/cost tradeoffs, and produce a machine-readable routing config that integrates with the smart-routing service. This ticket covers PM scope: PRD, acceptance criteria, UX sign-off, and rollout plan. Engineering and Design tickets will handle implementation details.
acceptance_criteria:
- Console exposes a Policy Studio accessible via Project Settings > Routing
- Users can author rules covering region preferences (e.g., prefer us-west, require eu-west for GDPR), tier routing (map customer tier to capacity pool), and fallback variants (model family -> variant chain)
- Inline validation flags conflicting or impossible rules (e.g., require eu-west and prefer us-west simultaneously)
- Preview pane renders deterministic example routing decisions for a sample request (region, tier, model) and shows estimated delta in latency and cost using recent telemetry
- Save produces a JSON policy that the backend accepts and that can be toggled on/off via rollout controls
- UI copies a stable permalink to the policy and surfaces linked audit log entries
- Documentation and quickstart in Console help are available on save
design_notes:
- Primary UX pattern: two-pane editor. Left: structured builder with rule blocks (conditions + actions). Right: live preview + validation feed + telemetry estimates.
- Use existing Console form components: multi-select region chips, tier dropdown, model-variant selector with inline thumbnails for model family and quantization level.
- Allow advanced users to switch to raw JSON mode with schema validation.
- Figma frames: 'Policy Studio - Builder', 'Policy Studio - Preview', 'Policy Studio - Conflict Modal' (links below).
- Accessibility: keyboard-first navigation for rule blocks and ARIA live region for validation messages.
engineering_notes:
- Backend contract: POST /v1/projects/:id/routing-policies should accept policy JSON and run server-side validation. See ENG-5121 for schema.
- Telemetry: use recent 30d token/latency/cost histograms to produce preview estimates. ENG-5189 to expose summarized metrics endpoint.
- Rollout hooks: saved policies must be feature-flag gated with canary percent and per-route overrides.
- Consider offline validation latency; front-end should do optimistic validation against JSON schema and fall back to server validation for cross-resource checks (e.g., availability of dedicated pools in region).
- Edge case: when a policy references an unavailable variant, show 'fallback to next candidate' and create a non-blocking audit event.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for validation UI and JSON roundtrip.
- E2E flows: create policy, simulate sample request in preview, save, toggle rollout, delete.
- Regression tests: ensure existing routing rules without policy studio continue to resolve.
- Performance: policy editor should load and validate a policy of 200 rules in <800ms on typical dev machine.
- Security: saved policies should be visible only to users with 'routing:write' role. Verify RBAC with an integration test.
rollout_plan:
- Alpha: enable for internal orgs + 3 pilot customers (support/SE notified).
- Beta: opt-in for all customers with Console seat and routing write permission; collect feedback & crash telemetry.
- GA: enable in all regions, link to public docs, and add onboarding checklist to Quickstart.
- Support: create a troubleshooting runbook for common validation errors and fallback behaviors.
